title: Observability Provenance Orchestrator: field-aware redaction + access ledger for traces and logs
creator: Samir Patel
description: Goal: Build a coordinated pipeline that enforces field-aware redaction and tenant-scoped retention for traces, logs, and select metric labels while recording a tamper-evident access ledger. This ticket implements: 1) trace-span tagging hooks so services can mark sensitive payloads at source; 2) a streaming redaction stage that applies field-level rules (PII regexes, customer allowlists, tokenization) across OTLP/log events; 3) retention enforcer that moves data through TTL tiers (hot -> warm -> scrubbed -> purge); 4) RBAC-backed query access ledger that logs who requested raw or unmasked records and supports just-in-time unmasking approval flow.
acceptance_criteria: Tracing SDKs emit an optional 'sensitivity' span attribute and a canonical 'provenance_id' for each trace that surfaces in downstream processors.

Streaming redaction stage strips or pseudonymizes configured sensitive fields in >99.9% of sampled test traces and logs according to rule-set v1 without increasing 95th percentile processing latency by >15%.
Retention enforcer honors tenant-configured TTLs: data older than 'scrub_after' is irreversibly pseudonymized and 'purge_after' triggers deletion; verified in integration tests.
Query access ledger records user id, query id, model of data requested (raw/masked), justification, and action outcome; entries are immutable and exportable for audits.
RBAC integration with SSO works end-to-end: users without 'raw_observability_read' receive masked results; users who request unmasking trigger approval workflow.
Operational runbook created with rollback steps and a diagnostic dashboard to verify redaction rates and request latency impact.
Security review completed and sign-off attached to the ticket.
implementation_notes: Instrument tracing SDKs (Go/Python/Node) to include 'provenance_id' and 'sensitivity' attributes. Provide opt-in libraries for partners to adopt.
Implement redaction as a streaming transform in the observability ingestion pipeline (sidecar-capable) using a rule engine; rules stored in tenant-scoped store with versioning.
Support three redaction modes per-field: remove, mask (consistent pseudonym), hash+salt (tenant-specific), plus configurable allowlist for developer-specified fields.
Retention controller runs periodic compaction jobs: moves older indices to scrubbed store and triggers async purge tasks; maintain tombstone markers for auditability.
Access ledger implemented as an append-only, signed log persisted to internal ledger storage. Ledger entries expose a read-only API for compliance exports.
Build a lightweight canary: enable strong redaction for 5% of tenant traffic and compare output to baseline to detect regressions.
Ensure redaction policy evaluations are testable via unit and integration tests (fuzzing inputs with synthetic PII patterns).
Plan for a soft-fallback: if redaction fails on a record, route to quarantine tier and surface to SRE with sample for manual inspection.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag scaffolding and SDK attribute additions (internal services only).
Phase 1: Deploy streaming redaction pipeline in staging; run canary at 5% of production traffic for non-critical tenants.
Phase 2: Open opt-in for customers to enable tenant redaction/ledger features; collect metrics and iterate on rule false positives.
Phase 3: Enforce retention policies for new tenants; offer migration tool for existing data to transition into retention tiers.
Phase 4: Full enforcement and default stricter redaction for system-level traces; monitor and adjust based on operational metrics.
testing_plan: Unit tests for rule engine (field patterns, allowlists, pseudonym consistency).
Integration tests across SDK -> ingestion -> redactor -> retention controller with synthetic PII datasets.
Load test to measure throughput and 95th/99th percentile latency impact; target <15% latency regression on ingestion path.
Chaos scenario: simulate redaction service downtime and verify quarantine and alerting behavior.
Compliance tests: export access ledger and demonstrate audit report generation for a sample subpoena request.
